editorial:
Imagine spending thirteen years in prison for a crime you might not have committed. That is exactly where you find the main character in this tense story. He is just trying to get his life back together, but two pushy film students won't leave him alone. They want to make a documentary about his past and the death of his high school girlfriend. The vibe is very uneasy from the start because you never quite know if you can trust the guy on screen or if the students are just being too nosey for their own good.

What really works here is how the tension builds slowly until it finally snaps. The acting feels real, and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. Some parts of the story move a bit slow, but the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy mysteries that make you question everything, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: The big twist reveals that the main character actually was the killer all along. He played the victims and the students to make himself look like an innocent man. In the final scenes, the film students realize they are in danger too late. He turns the tables on them in a violent way to keep his secret safe. The movie wraps up with him successfully hiding his true nature from the world once again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and shocking plot twists.
